properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 15 at 3:21PM CST until November 15 at 4:00PM CST by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
SMWHGX

The National Weather Service in League City has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Freeport to Matagorda Ship Channel TX out 20
NM...
Coastal waters from High Island to Freeport TX out 20 NM...
Galveston Bay...

* Until 400 PM CST.

* At 321 PM CST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near Surfside Jetty, moving east at 20
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts to nearly 50 knots, and small
hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Drum Bay and Surfside Jetty.
properties.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.areaDesc: Brazoria, TX
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 15 at 3:14PM CST until November 15 at 6:15PM CST by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Brazoria County in southeastern Texas...

* WHEN...Until 615 PM CST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 313 PM CST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 2 and 4
inches of rain have fallen in this area earlier today leading to
already saturated soils.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Southeastern Lake Jackson, Freeport, Clute, Surfside Beach,
Richwood, Jones Creek, Oyster Creek and San Luis Pass.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to
25 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor
beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock
people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid
ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 15 at 11:44AM PST until November 15 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 14 to 18 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 12 to 17 feet with local
sets to 20 feet and dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 3 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an
exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal
structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore. Minor tidal overflow during morning high
tides.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will
create an extended period of large surf this week, with the
potential for WARNING level surf Wednesday and Thursday. Areas
that may see most significant impacts will be west- northwest
facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely at low lying
areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the
Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor
entrance.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

* WHAT...For the Winter Weather Advisory, snow accumulations up to 6

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The

bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and
overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

Persons are urged to stay indoors until conditions improve. If you
must go outside, dress in layers. Several layers of clothes will keep
you warmer than a single heavy coat. Cover exposed skin to reduce
your risk of frostbite or hypothermia. Gloves, a scarf, and a hat
will keep you from losing your body heat.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 15 at 4:40AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Confidence is growing in the potential for a strong coastal storm
to take a more northerly track through the Bering Sea mid-week.
Depending on the final track of the system, minor to moderate
coastal flooding impacts may be a possible for parts of the West
Coast, with sea level rises between 3 to 7 ft possible. In
addition to the coastal impact potential, periods of moderate to
heavy snow and strong winds could begin as early as Tuesday night
and last into Friday. The combination of winds and heavy snow
could lead to reduced visibilities at times. We will continue to
monitor this system closely and provide updates as additional
information becomes available.

properties.areaDesc: Maui County Windward Waters; Big Island Windward Waters
properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 15 at 3:13AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
A moderate, long-period north swell from 350 to 360 degrees will
build across Hawaiian waters and peak later today and Monday as
the period shortens to 12 seconds. The swell will produce
moderate to heavy surges in north-facing harbors, especially at
Kahului and Hilo Harbors. Mariners using these harbors should
exercise caution when mooring or launching vessels and when
entering or leaving port. The swell will diminish Tuesday.

NWSheadline: SURGES AT KAHULUI AND HILO HARBORS TODAY AND MONDAY

* WHEN...From noon today to 4 AM PST Monday. .

properties.instruction:

run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 15 at 2:37AM HST until November 15 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
* WHAT...East winds 15 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph are
expected.

* WHERE...Portions of Oahu, Molokai, Lanai, Kahoolawe, Maui, and the
Big Island of Hawaii.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Winds this strong can tear off shingles, knock down tree
branches, blow away tents and awnings and make it difficult to
steer, especially for drivers of high profile vehicles.
properties.instruction:
Watch out for falling tree branches when walking or driving. Make
sure tents and awnings are secure or take them down. Be prepared for
power outages.

Use extra caution when driving, especially if operating a high
profile vehicle. Secure outdoor objects.

Brookings.

hazardous conditions along beaches and area shorelines. Waves

expected.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 15 at 3:43AM PST until November 17 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 20 to 25 ft, with occasional sets
of 25 to 35 ft at favored breakpoints.

* WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.
Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.
properties.instruction:
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

properties.description:
A large west to northwesterly swell will continue to produce
breaking waves at the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances
through at least this afternoon. These conditions have a history
of capsizing vessels of various sizes resulting in serious injury
or death, even to the most experienced mariners. Mariners are
urged to stay clear of these harbor entrances. For more
information, contact the local harbor patrol or coast guard
station and continue to monitor NOAA Weather Radio for the latest
weather information.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 15 at 2:27AM CST until November 17 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
3 to 8 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip
Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 PM this evening
to 6 AM CST Tuesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from this
evening through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide
at 1115 PM tonight and again at 1122 PM Monday night.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Maricopa, AZ; Yuma, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 13 at 7:24PM MST until November 17 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 724 PM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow peaking at 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream  also indicated a stage of 9.93 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING FOR THE UPSTREAM RELEASE OF PAINTED ROCK DAM ON THE GILA RIVER REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 AM MST TUESDAY
